items.title: Barry Kernfeld interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 16, 2020
items.q: "maybe it was in Buffalo with Al Sears or something like that." ... "These people were classmates. They went to school together."

ctx.x: Yes, we’re working on that now. I would say that insofar as it’s possible to check primary sources, which now with Ancestry includes a huge wealth of genealogical documents, and family blogs, family trees, things like that. So that helps sort things out. Musicians’ unions reports, so-and-so traveled here, record company catalogues. And what we found doing the Grove because jazz is this small, small world of interlocking relationships. And what we did with Grove that I think no one else had done was to check…

bands, where they played, look at the history of the clubs, look at the band lists, and when it disagreed you might get the same thing nineteen times and find the right one on the twentieth, and that the other nineteen were just copying from each other. We tried to cross check just exhaustively in every source that we could get our hands at, whether it’s a written document, iconography, photographs. So that’s part of your answer. I would like to say, you know, something about why. Because people might think that…
